text: Right now, your body is making millions of new cells, to help you grow and to repair any damage.
It makes them by mitosis: one cell dividing into two identical cells.
But here's the bit people get wrong. The cell copies its DNA before mitosis even starts.
Each chromosome becomes two identical copies, joined in the middle.
Then mitosis begins. The chromosomes line up across the middle of the cell.
Fibres pull the copies apart, one to each end, and the nucleus divides.
Finally the cytoplasm and cell membrane split, and there are two new cells, each with exactly the same chromosomes as the first.
Quick check. Does the cell copy its DNA before mitosis, or during it?
Before. That's why both new cells get a full set.
